Ethiopian shelling of Tigray town should be investigated as possible war crimes, Amnesty says

Reuters

24 November, 2026 10:30 am IST

By Vincent Mumo Nzilani NAIROBI, Nov 24 (Reuters) – Amnesty International said on Tuesday that artillery strikes by Ethiopian forces and a pro-government militia on densely populated urban areas in the northern Tigray region this year should be investigated as possible war crimes.

The human rights group also accused the rebel Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) of endangering civilians during the September battle for the town of Alamata by placing fighters in residential areas and using local schools for military purposes.

The eruption of fighting on September 23 between pro-government forces and the TPLF rekindled a 2020-2022 civil war, in which the United States accused all sides of committing war crimes. The warring parties all denied allegations of widespread abuses.

Show Full Article

Spokespeople for the Ethiopian government, the Ethiopian National Defence Force (ENDF) and the TPLF did not respond to Reuters requests for comment on the Amnesty report.

Amnesty said the TPLF provided it with a written response that said the allegations against the group were unfounded.

A spokesperson for the Tigray Peace Force (TPF), a pro-government militia that Amnesty said was involved in shelling Alamata, told Reuters that the group’s fighters were not on the front lines during the battle.

AMNESTY ACCUSES ETHIOPIAN FORCES OF ‘TOTAL DISREGARD’ FOR CIVILIAN LIVES

Amnesty, which based its report on interviews with survivors and witnesses and on videos, satellite imagery and other open-source material, said the ENDF and TPF shelled residential areas of Alamata, in southern Tigray, while advancing on the town.

“For three consecutive days, the ENDF and TPF repeatedly shelled Alamata in total disregard of the lives of its 80,000 inhabitants,” Yasmine Ahmed, Amnesty’s senior director for regional human rights impact, said.

The ENDF and TPF seized Alamata on September 28 and captured Tigray’s capital Mekelle less than a week later.

Federal forces now control major cities across Tigray but continue to face resistance from TPLF fighters. Ethiopia and neighbouring Eritrea, which lies north of Tigray, have also been amassing forces along their shared border in recent days, according to conflict monitors and people tied to Tigrayan militias, fuelling fears of outright war between the historical rivals.

Ethiopia and Eritrea have not directly commented on the troop build-up.

The 2020-2022 civil war in Tigray was one of this century’s deadliest, killing around 600,000 people, according to the African Union. There have been no comprehensive estimates of the current conflict’s human toll.

FIVE HOUSES HIT IN ONE NEIGHBOURHOOD

In Alamata, Amnesty said it had independently verified the deaths of 14 civilians and many more injuries in four shelling incidents.

One of the deadliest struck five houses in the Kebele 04 residential area on September 27, killing seven people, including a mother, her young son and her brother.

Amnesty said the strikes hit homes about 150 metres (490 feet) from the Werknesh Hotel. Some residents said the hotel had housed TPLF fighters, though Amnesty said it could not verify whether they were there at the time of the attack.

Amnesty said the presence of TPLF fighters nearby could not justify the indiscriminate use of explosive weapons in a densely populated area.

(Reporting by Vincent Mumo Nzilani; Editing by Aaron Ross and Xevi Fontdegloria)

Trump to meet NATO chief Mark Rutte on Wednesday, White House says

By Kanishka Singh WASHINGTON, Nov 23 (Reuters) – US President Donald Trump will meet NATO chief Mark Rutte on Wednesday in Florida, the White House said on Monday, with the meeting coming after the Republican leader met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping last week in Asia.

• The White House said Trump and Rutte will meet late in the afternoon on Wednesday in Palm Beach, Florida.

• Trump, who has been critical of America’s Western allies, cast both Putin and Xi as his “friend” when he met them last week at a summit.

Show Full Article

• Trump’s meeting with Putin triggered a backlash among both European allies and Trump’s Democratic opponents at home.

• Rutte, who has repeatedly tried to soothe tensions within NATO and keep Trump onside, said it was normal for major nuclear powers to meet.

• Rutte’s meeting with Trump also comes as Europe has pushed to be included in US-backed talks to end Russia’s war in Ukraine.

• Trump has often criticized Washington’s Western and democratic allies over issues like NATO spending, trade tariffs and what he casts as their inadequate support for Washington during the US-Israeli war on Iran.

• Trump was open to security guarantees for Ukraine based on the NATO alliance’s Article 5 mutual defense agreement, and that Russia had grown “comfortable” with that, US special envoy and Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner said last week as he sought to reassure allies.

• Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, who has been criticized by Trump, has said Europe had to be included in peace talks.

(Reporting by Kanishka Singh in Washington; editing by Lincoln Feast.)

South Korea issues ‘take shelter’ warning after Russia aircraft fly near airspace

Reuters

24 November, 2026 09:00 am IST

By Jack Kim SEOUL, Nov 24 (Reuters) – South Korea’s Air Force scrambled fighter jets on Tuesday and the government issued a “preemptive” warning to take shelter for residents of an island after Russian military planes briefly entered the country’s air defense identification zone (ADIZ).

South Korea’s military had tracked “multiple” Russian aircraft as they made the approach and were “on the verge” of entering the airspace over Ulleung island off the east coast, a spokesperson for the Joint Chiefs of Staff said.

“Airspace intrusion was anticipated, therefore in order to protect the safety of our people, we issued a warning preemptively,” Jang Do-young told a briefing.

Show Full Article

There was no intrusion of South Korea’s airspace by the Russian aircraft in the end, the military said.

The defence ministry will summon the Russian military attache later on Tuesday to “lodge a stern protest,” ministry spokesperson Chung Binna said.

The Russian embassy in Seoul did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

An ADIZ is an area set by countries to help identify and respond to any aircraft that may be approaching their airspace.

Russian aircraft have entered South Korea’s ADIZ several times in recent months as Moscow does not recognize the designation, but the civil defense warning telling residents to urgently take shelter was rare.

A civil defense warning issued earlier by the Safety Ministry in coordination with the military advised residents of Ulleung island to take shelter due to “airspace intrusion” by Russian aircraft. It was lifted three minutes later.

Jang, the military spokesperson, said the aircraft came “very close” to the airspace above Ulleung island.

South Korean fighter jets conducted “tactical maneuvers” to prevent any incident, the Joint Chiefs of Staff said.

A separate warning was issued in error by the area’s provincial government that an aircraft suspected to be North Korean had entered the area, before it was withdrawn.

(Reporting by Jack Kim, Kyu-seok Shim; Editing by David Gregorio and Lincoln Feast.)
